diagnostic_evidence.quote: Summing over the lattice ensures $G_{\textrm{per}}(z)$ to be doubly-periodic.
There is no doubly-periodic Green's function satisfying \(\Delta G(z) = -\delta(z)\) as integrating both sides and applying Green's theorem yields a contradiction

issues.failure_explanation: The summands do not tend to zero as the lattice point tends to infinity; they tend to minus infinity. Thus the displayed sum does not define a function, and reindexing it cannot establish periodicity. A regularization and the neutralizing background are essential.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the lattice expression as a formal periodization requiring regularization, and distinguish it from the well-defined background-corrected Green's function already supplied in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory definition and description of the conventional periodic Green's function are mathematically incorrect. The later theta-function definition is independent of this sum.
issues.title: The unregularized logarithmic lattice sum is divergent
issues.why_classification: A local qualification using the paper's existing Green's function preserves the developed method and all its substantive results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The fluid velocity is given by $\nabla \phi$
A_j  := \int_{\partial D_j}  \partial_\nu u (z) \, |dz|= \int_{\partial D_j} \partial_\sigma v(z) \, |dz|, \qquad j \in [M].

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed integral is the tangential circulation of the gradient. For a single-valued velocity potential it is zero around every closed curve, even when the normal flux is nonzero. It therefore cannot represent the hole fluxes used in the other viewpoints and the main theorems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the circulation integral by the normal-flux integral, or equivalently the appropriate tangential increment of the stream function, consistently with the previously defined A_j.
issues.overall_effect: The fluid-dynamical explanation does not describe the nonzero flux coefficients computed by the layer-potential method.
issues.title: The fluid flux is defined as circulation rather than normal flux
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the differential being integrated; it does not alter the layer-potential results or computations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: pointing outward from \( \Omega \) (i.e., pointing into \( D_j \))
The fluid velocity is given by $\nabla \phi$

issues.failure_explanation: With velocity equal to the gradient and ν pointing into a hole, positive normal flux means fluid enters that hole: it is a sink, not a source. This sign error remains after replacing the erroneous circulation formula by the correct normal-flux formula.

failure_location.quote: If $A_j >0$, we interpret $D_j$ to be a source of the fluid and if $A_j<0$, we interpret $D_j$ to be a sink.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the source/sink descriptions, or explicitly define outward-from-hole physical flux as minus A_j without changing the mathematical convention.
issues.overall_effect: The physical source/sink interpretation, including the description of one source and two sinks, has its signs reversed relative to the mathematical coefficients.
issues.title: The source and sink signs contradict the prescribed normal
issues.why_classification: A local orientation correction preserves the computed coefficients and all boundary-value results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, $\Im f_\mathcal{D}[\phi]$ is not necessarily doubly-periodic

issues.failure_explanation: Hole periods do not exhaust the first cohomology of a punctured torus. For example, on a square torus with a small disk removed, dx is a harmonic closed form with zero integral around the hole but nonzero integral around a torus generator, so it is not exact. There are two handle periods in addition to the M−1 independent hole periods.

failure_location.quote: Similarly, a harmonic differential 1-form on $\Omega$ is closed, so de Rham cohomology allows us to express it as the sum of an exact form and a term that accounts for the non-trivial integral around each  hole, $D_j$, $j\in [M]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the two torus-generator cohomology classes and distinguish their periods from the M−1 independent boundary-component fluxes.
issues.overall_effect: The conceptual account incorrectly suggests that hole fluxes account for all obstructions to a single-valued conjugate. The later allowance for quasiperiodic conjugates does not make this earlier description correct.
issues.title: The cohomological description omits the two torus-cycle periods
issues.why_classification: The claimed decomposition is missing two independent degrees of freedom. Correcting it requires a substantive but contained topological revision, without changing the main layer-potential architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The quantity $A_j$ can be interpreted as the flux across $\partial D_j$,  $j\in [M]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Continuous Dirichlet data do not guarantee an integrable classical boundary normal derivative. Such solutions can have only distributional Neumann traces. The proof nevertheless uses the pointwise limiting derivative and its boundary integral without establishing their existence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define total flux using a smooth homologous contour inside Ω, or an appropriate weak trace, and identify it with the classical boundary integral when the Dirichlet data have sufficient regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The classical boundary-integral interpretation of A_j is unsupported at the theorem's stated regularity, although the representation and a generalized total flux can remain valid.
issues.title: Classical boundary flux is used for arbitrary continuous Dirichlet data
issues.why_classification: The interior-contour interpretation is a local Green-identity repair that preserves the theorem for all continuous data and retains the same flux coefficients.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We further assume that each hole \( D_j \) has a \( C^2 \) boundary, \( \partial D_j \).

issues.failure_explanation: The standing assumption permits boundaries that are not smooth beyond order two. Steklov boundary regularity is limited by the geometry; arbitrary-order smoothness of the traces is not available under this assumption. The paper supplies no stronger geometric hypothesis for this assertion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the boundary-basis property in L² with the finite regularity available under the standing assumptions, and reserve C∞ regularity for smooth boundaries.
issues.overall_effect: The stated C∞ regularity is not justified for the advertised domain class. The spectral enumeration and the layer-potential formulation do not require this overstatement.
issues.title: Infinite smoothness of Steklov traces is asserted on only C² boundaries
issues.why_classification: This requires a genuine weakening of the asserted regularity, but leaves the spectral and boundary-integral results recognizably unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that the fixed \(\gamma > 0\) is small enough so that we can express $z = z_0-h\nu(z_0) \in \partial\Omega$, for $h = \vert z- z_0 \vert$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimates are made only along the normal through a fixed boundary point. Interior continuity does not imply that a normal boundary limit is the unrestricted limit along every approach. The stated jump relation therefore needs an additional uniform boundary argument.

failure_location.quote: We only need to consider for such $z$ since $\mathcal{D}[\phi]$ is continuous on $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the normal-limit estimates uniform in the boundary base point using compactness and uniform continuity of φ, then use nearest-point projection and continuity of the proposed boundary trace to handle arbitrary approaches.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish the full boundary continuity needed for the Dirichlet representation and subsequent uniqueness arguments.
issues.title: Normal convergence is incorrectly promoted to an unrestricted boundary limit
issues.why_classification: The existing estimates support a short uniformization argument; no new substantive lemma or change of conclusion is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed unrestricted identity makes the potential zero on Ω. The proof establishes only that it is constant on each closed hole. For a nonzero nullspace density, continuity, uniqueness on the complementary regions, and the normal-derivative jump rule rule out the asserted global indicator-function representation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the identity to the union of the closed holes, or replace it by the componentwise statement proved in equation eqn: sjk.
issues.overall_effect: Part (5) contains a false global support claim. Later arguments use only the valid values inside the holes, so they are not invalidated by this overstatement.
issues.title: The nullspace single-layer potentials are wrongly asserted to vanish outside the holes
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws a substantive global identity while preserving the useful componentwise characterization and basis conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The normal-vector calculation produces an oriented complex differential dξ, but the defined potential replaces it by |dξ| and loses the unit-tangent factor. Consequently its real part is not the double layer and its jump is not the stated real density jump. For φ=1, its real increment under z↦z+τ is minus the boundary length, whereas the double layer is periodic.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb T_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use dξ in the Cauchy-type term of the complex potential and the associated Cauchy formulas, consistently with the oriented-differential expression already derived in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The complex representation used to prove the double-layer nullspace characterization and characteristic-operator invertibility is incorrect as defined.
issues.title: Arclength is substituted for the complex contour differential
issues.why_classification: The source already contains the corrected representation. Restoring its differential is a local construction repair that preserves the intended conclusions, apart from the independent trace-regularity issue.

issues.failure_explanation: Continuity alone does not ensure existence of the Cauchy principal value or finite boundary limits at every point. In a local boundary coordinate, a continuous density proportional to sign(t)/log(e/|t|) produces a divergent principal-value contribution proportional to the integral of 1/(t log(e/t)). This failure persists after correcting dξ.

failure_location.quote: The result directly follows from the Sokhotski-Plemelj formula \cite[Thm. 7.8]{kress1989linear}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the pointwise jump theorem for Dini-continuous or Hölder densities and establish that the homogeneous densities used later have this regularity. The C² kernel estimates can support the needed smoothing bootstrap.
issues.overall_effect: Part (2) is false for its stated density class, and its uses for the homogeneous densities in the nullspace proofs require additional regularity justification.
issues.title: Pointwise Plemelj limits are asserted for every continuous density
issues.why_classification: A restricted trace statement and a contained regularity lemma are needed to preserve the main continuous-data boundary-value results.

issues.failure_explanation: Since z−conjugate(z)=2i Im(z), the quadratic term is −Im(z)²/(2b), not positive. Thus the proposed real part differs from G by −Im(z)²/b and has the wrong off-singularity Laplacian. The proof explicitly relies on the erroneous squaring identity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the sign of the quadratic term in f_G and correct the real-part calculation.
issues.overall_effect: Part (3) does not supply the asserted complex representation of the specified Green's function.
issues.title: The proposed complex Green function has the wrong quadratic real part
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the construction and its calculation restores the claimed representation, with no downstream argument using this erroneous part.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the representation and normalization, not a continuously differentiable boundary trace. The tangential derivative of a single-layer trace contains a Hilbert-transform singularity, which need not be continuous or finite for continuous densities. Taking a continuous non-Dini mean-zero density ψ and g=(D*+I/2)ψ gives a continuous admissible Neumann datum without the asserted C¹ trace.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use C₀ as the codomain at the stated input regularity, or impose sufficient Hölder/Dini regularity on the input for the stronger conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed codomain is too strong. The formula itself and its use in the Steklov representation do not require this C¹ conclusion.
issues.title: The Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is assigned an unjustified C¹ range
issues.why_classification: A genuine regularity conclusion must be weakened or its hypotheses strengthened, but the operator formula and subsequent eigenproblem remain available.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The holes \(D_j \subset \mathbb C \), for \(j \in [M]\) are open, simply-connected sets

issues.failure_explanation: Both maps take only real values. Their images are subsets of a line, not closed planar curves enclosing the asserted holes; the centers are not added and no angular direction is supplied. Consequently these formulas cannot define the numerical domains or the curvature used in their discretizations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify genuine periodic polar parametrizations, such as θ↦a_i+ρ_i(θ)e^(−iθ), with the intended radial profiles, and verify that the reported domains and numerical results use those parametrizations.
issues.overall_effect: The noncircular domains in Examples 2, 3, and 6 and their stated numerical constructions are not defined by the supplied formulas.
issues.title: The hole parametrizations are real-valued radial profiles, not boundary curves
issues.why_classification: The numerical geometry needs an actual corrected construction and verification, but the intended radial-hole family and layer-potential method can be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using an aposteriori estimate, the eigenvalue approximations have a relative error less than $10^{-14}$.
The eigenpairs $(\sigma, \vec{\phi})$ are computed using MATLAB's built-in function \texttt{eig}.

issues.failure_explanation: A residual at the same collocation nodes used to solve the matrix eigenproblem can be zero in exact arithmetic regardless of the continuum discretization error. No estimate controls the residual between nodes or the error in boundary reconstruction and quadrature. Consequently the sampled residual does not certify the claimed continuum eigenvalue accuracy.

failure_location.quote: We note that the aposteriori error calculated by $\Vert\partial_\nu u_k(z)-\sigma_k u_k(z)\Vert_{\infty}$ at each grid point can be used to bound relative errors in $\sigma_k$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must independently bound the continuum boundary residual, including reconstruction and quadrature errors, and apply a normalized spectral error bound to that residual.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed relative-error certification for Example 6 and Figure fig:many holes is unsupported; the reported numbers can be matrix residuals rather than eigenvalue-error bounds.
issues.title: Collocation residuals are treated as certified eigenvalue errors
issues.why_classification: The source does not supply the information needed to recover the advertised accuracy certification. Reporting only collocation residuals would abandon that substantive guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The system has a unique solution due to Theorem~\ref{thm: neumann}.

issues.failure_explanation: Invertibility of a continuous integral equation does not imply invertibility of an arbitrary Nyström matrix. There is an explicit allowed counterexample: for one circular hole with one trapezoidal node, κ=−1/r and h=2πr, so D=1/2 and D−I/2 is the zero matrix. The analogous appeal to the continuous Neumann theorem also supplies no discrete stability argument.

failure_location.quote: The system has a unique solution due to Theorem~\ref{thm: dirichlet}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish Nyström stability for sufficiently fine grids and state the required resolution condition, rather than inferring finite-dimensional invertibility directly from the continuous theorems.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional discrete uniqueness claims are false or unsupported, even though the continuous boundary-value theorems can be valid.
issues.title: Continuous invertibility is used to assert invertibility of every discrete system
issues.why_classification: A contained discretization-stability argument and a resolution-dependent qualification are required; the numerical method need not be replaced.

issues.failure_explanation: Both Nyström matrices attach the quadrature weight to the source column. Transposing D moves that weight to the target row. If H is the diagonal matrix of the h-weights, the correct identity is D_s=H^(-1)D^T H, not D_s=D^T, except when all weights coincide.

failure_location.quote: Note that \( D_s = D^T \), where $D$ is defined in Appendix~\ref{s: dirichlet num implementation}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the transpose assertion by the weighted-adjoint identity and use either that identity or the explicitly defined D_s entries in implementation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated transpose shortcut is wrong for nonuniform arclength weights, including irregular holes and components of different sizes. The separately displayed weighted kernel matrix can still be correct.
issues.title: The Nyström adjoint is not the ordinary matrix transpose
issues.why_classification: A local weighted-transpose correction preserves the stated continuous and discrete formulations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we use a uniform grid, i.e., setting \(s^k_j = \frac{2\pi j}{N_k}\).

issues.failure_explanation: This is an even-node Fourier product rule, but N_k is not restricted to be even. For odd N_k its final frequency is half-integral, so the weights are not periodic. At grid nodes it even gives a nonzero result of order N_k^(-2) for constant data, whose exact logarithmic integral is zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every N_k to be even, as in the reported examples, or provide the separate odd-node Fourier rule.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed singular quadrature and spectral behavior do not extend to the allowed odd node counts.
issues.title: The logarithmic product rule is invalid for odd node counts
issues.why_classification: An explicit even-node input condition is a standard local repair and preserves all reported examples and the intended method.

issues.failure_explanation: R_j already contains the integration weight for dt. To integrate the boundary density, it should multiply |z'(t_j)|φ_j, not h_jφ_j=w_j|z'(t_j)|φ_j. The displayed matrix inserts an extra trapezoidal factor 2π/N_k, so its singular contribution tends to zero instead of the required logarithmic operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace h^k_j in the S^k_1 block by |z^{k\prime}(s^k_j)|, leaving the ordinary trapezoidal weights in S^k_2 and the off-diagonal blocks, and verify the numerical outputs with the corrected assembly.
issues.overall_effect: The assembled S matrix does not converge to the single-layer boundary operator. The Steklov discretization and boundary evaluations using this matrix are therefore inconsistent as written.
issues.title: The singular single-layer quadrature is weighted twice
issues.why_classification: The source's own product-integration formula determines a short local weight correction; no new quadrature construction or change of intended rate is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side should contain S(I−M)+M. As written, both matrices annihilate the constant vector, so every σ paired with a constant density satisfies the pencil, while the reconstructed function is the nonzero constant and satisfies the Steklov condition only for σ=0. The pencil is singular and is not the discrete analogue of the theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (D_s+I/2)(I−M)φ=σ[S(I−M)+M]φ, consistently retain the constant mode, and verify the numerical outputs using that pencil.
issues.overall_effect: The stated eig call has an indeterminate common-nullspace problem and does not deliver the advertised Steklov eigenpairs, including the correctly represented zero mode.
issues.title: The discrete Steklov pencil omits the constant part of the modified single layer
issues.why_classification: The missing rank-one term is supplied explicitly by the continuous formulation and reconstruction. Restoring it is a local matrix-assembly repair, not a new eigenvalue method.
